request: How does a transformer turn the words in a sentence into embeddings?

composition.story: Tokens enter the transformer, converting text into dense continuous vectors. Positional encoding adds sequence order. Self-attention weights contextual relationships across all words simultaneously, producing final enriched embeddings for downstream tasks.

aha.observation: Self-attention computes dot products between queries and keys, routing information dynamically between unrelated words based on context.

states.label: Tokenize
states.sentence: The raw sentence is split into discrete subword tokens.
states.why: Mapping words to integer IDs prepares text for numerical lookup.

states.label: Embed
states.sentence: Each token ID fetches a high-dimensional vector from the embedding table.
states.why: Converts discrete symbols into continuous semantic space.

states.label: Position
states.sentence: Sinusoidal positional encodings are added to retain word order.
states.why: Transformers process sets, so explicit position prevents loss of syntax.

states.label: Attention
states.sentence: Queries, keys, and values compute weighted sums across all token vectors.
states.why: Resolves polysemy by blending contextual semantics into each vector.

states.label: Output
states.sentence: The resulting context-aware vectors emerge as final embeddings.
states.why: Ready for classification, generation, or retrieval tasks.
